text:
alex: heads-up — saw a regression on the long-seq mixed workload on prod-rt-3. throughput drops ~25% and HBM BW looks spiky. filing here before diving in.

samira: can you paste the nsys output or perfetto? curious if it's a kernel hot loop or straight memory saturation.

alex: attaching quick nsys summary from the run (trimmed):\n```\n== NVTX API tracing start ==\nElapsed GPU time (ms): 5234.2\nHBM throughput peak: 740 GB/s\nDRAM busy % (timeline avg): 88%\nTop kernels by GPU time:\n  - aten::matmul (float32 fallback) 42%\n  - kv_cache_read (small pages) 18%\n  - aten::softmax 9%\nKV cache hit-rate (per-request): median 94% but long-seq mix tail drops to 45%\nEviction spikes aligned with ~128-256 token sequences interleaved with short (8-16) sequences\n```\n
alex: perfetto link: https://perfetto.dev/trace/abcd1234 (private) — timeline shows repeated bursts of page migrations + dma stalls when seq switches from short->long.

nguyen: interesting. my first guess: the microbatching heuristic is compacting requests into batches that cause large working sets, but the runtime's KV prefetch/pinning assumes more locality. when interleaved short and long sequences, it repeatedly evicts small-page hot entries, then re-prefetches for long seq -> thrash.

samira: do we have a reproducer? if so we should run with KV debug counters + pinning disabled to confirm.

alex: yes repro script in infra/harnesses/longseq-mix.sh — used --batch_window=16 --microbatch=4. command i ran: `./repro.sh --model redwood-12b --seq-mix=interleave:8,256 --qps=60 --duration=10m`\n

jess: quick thought — kernel selection may be falling back to float32 GEMM for the long sequences due to a quantization path bug when kv pages are > N; float path uses more bandwidth and exacerbates HBM pressure. check kernel logs for quant fallback events.

perf-bot: automated-check: found 12 quantization fallbacks during trace (timestamps aligned with eviction spikes). See /var/log/prof/prof-1765004321.log

nguyen: ok that matches — eviction -> re-prefetch -> quant fallback -> bigger kernels -> more BW -> more eviction. vicious circle.

samira: steps: 1) rerun with microbatching off to see if thrash reduces 2) force quantized kernels for long seq to see impact 3) turn on KV pinning for last-N requests to test stopper

alex: did a quick experiment: disabled microbatch (window=1) for 2 minutes — throughput recovered to baseline, HBM avg down to 420 GB/s and KV hit-rate stayed ~92%. So microbatching heuristic is amplifying it.

jess: can you dump the runtime config that chose kernel? paste nvprof kernel name mapping (or the runtime's kernel selection log). also capture `nvidia-smi dmon` + `nvlink` counters.

alex: kernel selection excerpt: `choose_kernel(gemm_size=6144, quant_available=false) -> aten::matmul:f32_kernel_v2`\nquant fallback log snippet: `Quantizer::validate_table() failed for layer 23 -> fallback float32`\n

nguyen: hypothesis: when KV pages are evicted and then reloaded, some auxiliary metadata used for quant table validity isn't populated in time, causing conservative fallback. Two possible fixes: 1) ensure quant metadata is persisted with pinned KV pages, or 2) change microbatching to preserve a tiny warm set across batches (pin 'recent' pages for N ms).

samira: performance test plan: create 3 runs on staging-rt-4: baseline microbatch=16, microbatch=1, microbatch=16+pin_recent=8 (pin the last 8 requests' KV pages). Collect: nsys, KV hit-rate histogram, HBM BW, quant-fallback count. 10 min runs.

jess: also run an instrumented build that emits kernel selection traces to stdout (already in feature branch kern-trace). might be good to correlate exact call that falls back.

alex: I'll kick off those 3 runs now. attaching the command I used to capture counters: \n```\nnsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=cpu --output=run1 \
  --capture-range=nvtx --statistics true --force-overwrite \
  -- ./repro.sh --model redwood-12b --seq-mix=interleave:8,256 --batch_window=16 --duration=600\n```\n
nguyen: for the pinning experiment add `--kv-pin-recent=8` and enable `--kv-debug=1` to dump hit/evict logs.

perf-bot: scheduled job id 64211 for runs on staging-rt-4. you will get alerts when complete.

samira: if staging confirms, we should backport a short-term mitigation to prod: either reduce default microbatch window for mixed-seq customers or enable kv-pin-recent fallback on autoscale nodes.

jess: agree. long-term we need to fix the quant metadata population race during KV page load.

alex: update: first two runs finished. delta: microbatch=1 -> throughput +22% vs microbatch=16, HBM avg 430 GB/s. microbatch=16+pin_recent=8 -> throughput +15%, HBM avg 480 GB/s. quant-fallback count: 12 -> 2 with pinning.

nguyen: pinning helps but not full. points to both heuristics + quant metadata ordering.

samira: okay let's open an RFC: "kv-warmset-pin + quant-meta-sync" and propose emergency prod change: set microbatch default to 8 for mixed-seq customers and enable kv-pin-recent=4 on all dedicated pools for next 48h. I'll draft.

alex: logging follow-up: i'll attach perf logs and perfetto after processing. also created bug=RT-5032 for quant metadata race and assigned to @jess.

jess: i'll take RT-5032. thanks for triage. ping me when you have the kernel trace output.

alex: done — upload to: s3://redwood-perf/rt/1765004321/{nsys.zip,perfetto.pb,kv-debug.log}

samira: great thread. next step: implement config change and monitor 1h. :thumbsup:

jess: assigning myself to the quant fix, nguyen please follow up on pinning perf overhead numbers.

alex: closing loop here in an hour after we validate prod knobs. thanks team :)
